title: Streaming callback orchestrator with recursion throttles and structured-output validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a runtime-level orchestrator for multi-tool/function call chains that supports streaming responses, enforces structured-output schemas, and prevents runaway recursion or tool-injection loops. This ticket covers the server-side coordinator, session-level invocation graph, idempotency/ack protocol for streaming tool results, and a compatibility shim for older SDK clients that do not support incremental function callbacks. Goal: preserve low-latency streaming while ensuring safety (bounded loops), predictable cost, and deterministic structured outputs for downstream consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Server can interleave streamed LLM tokens with tool invocation events and deliver a single monotonic event stream to clients (tokens, tool-calls, tool-results, structured-output checkpoints)

A session-level recursion counter prevents more than N tool-invocations along any causal chain (configurable, default N=6) and triggers graceful fallback behavior (error token + final structured output) when exceeded
Structured-output schemas declared in model prompt or API call are validated at runtime; malformed tool results are rejected and retried up to M times, with clear diagnostics in response metadata
Compatibility shim routes legacy SDK clients through a deterministic buffered mode (no incremental tool events) while preserving existing API semantics
End-to-end tests cover: simple streaming generation, single tool call, multi-tool chains with streaming, loop detection triggered, and legacy SDK compatibility path
Telemetry captures: distribution of chain lengths, loop abort counts, average added latency for streaming tool events, and frequency of schema validation failures
design_notes: Key idea: treat the execution loop as a directed acyclic invocation graph per user session. Each tool invocation is a node with a unique invocation id and parent id(s). Streaming responses are composed of three logical event types: TOKEN, CALL_EVENT, CALL_RESULT. Clients receive an ordered event stream (RFC-like framing) and reconstruct the final structured output when a terminal event is emitted. To avoid infinite loops, maintain a per-session recursion fingerprint set (invocation signature: tool_id + normalized_args) and a hop counter. If a repeated signature occurs beyond threshold, emit a loop sentinel event and switch to fallback model variant (safer, smaller context) or return an engineered error object. For compatibility, legacy clients receive the same final events but with server-side buffering until completion; new clients opt in to incremental events via a query param or SDK flag.
implementation_plan: Wire session orchestration layer: session metadata with invocation_graph, recursion_counter, signature_set
Add event framing to streaming path: prefix bytes indicating event type and JSON payload (backwards-compatible with current streaming tokens scheme)
Tool runner changes: make tool results attach invocation_id and schema metadata; offer idempotent replay for retries
Loop detection: compute stable signature (sha256 of tool_id + canonicalized args + optional model_anchor). Maintain LRU set with TTL per session
Compatibility shim: server buffer path that reconstructs single final payload for legacy clients; SDK flag to request incremental stream
Structured-output validation: integrate JSON schema validator in post-tool-result step and emit diagnostics with path to failing field
Expose config knobs (per-org): max_chain_length, allow_recursion, fallback_model, schema_strictness
Unit + integration tests and add telemetry hooks for histograms and counters
tests: Unit: invocation_graph operations (add node, detect cycle, prune)
Integration: streaming pipeline with interleaved tool calls (simulate slow tool returning after tokens)
Regression: reproduce previously observed recursive-invocation bug and validate sentinel triggers
Compatibility: simulate legacy SDK consumption (buffered) and new SDK (incremental) and assert parity of final output
Load: synthetic workload to verify perf impact of recursion checks at 95th percentile latency
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + e2e tests in CI. 2) Canary on dedicated staging cluster with synthetic agents for 48h. 3) Gradual rollout to 5% hosted traffic with feature flag. 4) Monitor loop-abort rate, schema-failure rate, and user-observed token-latency. 5) If metrics stable for 24h, promote to 25% then 100% within 72h. Provide kill-switch that disables recursion checking and falls back to existing behavior in emergency.
risks: Added per-session bookkeeping costs could increase memory pressure under high concurrency
Buffering for legacy clients increases tail latency and cost; need strict canary and cost estimate
False-positive loop detection for legitimate repeated tool-use patterns (e.g., retries) — mitigated via signature heuristic and per-tool allowlist
Structured validation may surface many customer schema mismatches leading to poor UX unless error messages are actionable
